title.narrative: Guangxi Modern Technical and Vocational Education and Training Development Program

description.narrative: The program will provide, in 2017-2022, timely and essential support for the establishment of a technical and vocational education and training (TVET) system that provides graduates with better employment opportunities in industries in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region (GZAR) by enhancing the industry relevance of TVET, improving the quality of TVET, increasing the inclusiveness of TVET, and expanding the role of TVET in regional economic development. The proposed results-based lending (RBL) program is critical for GZAR to implement a comprehensive TVET system reform package with a focus on results and system improvements, in accordance with the GZAR's Thirteenth Five-Year Plan, 2016-2020, which is in the second year of implementation. It is expected to create strong synergetic effects, together with the Guangxi Regional Cooperation and Integration Promotion Investment Program, on cross-border cooperation and training, particularly benefiting bordering Viet Nam.

description.narrative: A TVET system that provides graduates with better employment opportunities in GZAR?'s industries established

Percentage of TVET graduates who stayed in their first job for more than 6 months increased to 54% (2016 baseline: 49% of TVET graduates) (DLI 1) Achievement: 54 Progress/Status: All targets have been achieved. However, continued monitoring would be useful to reflect impacts of COVID-19 on job stability and ensure sustainable intervention on TVET systems. GED agreed to allocate budget to monitor this indicator. Results of this indicator will provide insights to GED's policy and strategy for their graduate career development. Data Source: GED's management information system; GED's reports; reports of an independent third party

Percentage of TVET graduates who have dual certification increased to 72% (2016 baseline: 67% of TVET graduates) Achievement: 56.48 Progress/Status: By the end of 2022, the percentage of tertiary TVET graduates was 23.6%, against 37.0% in 2021, 47.64% in 2020 and 56.35% in 2019; while the percentage of second TVET graduates was 47.3%, against 50.5% in 2021, 56.48% in both 2020 and 2019. The decreasing trend results from (i) large cancellation of certification, and (ii) increasing promotion of students from secondary schools to tertiary colleges which results in lack of interest in applying for certification for secondary school students (dual certification is a requirement for graduation from secondary schools). Data Source: GED's management information system; GED's reports
